atlas-qa.0054: Lusail University Career Fair: 22–23 October 2025, its third edition, under the patronage of the Minister of Labour, who launched the university’s link to Ouqoul.
atlas-qa.0055: Big Four graduate roles in Doha may be sponsored by the local firm, unlike Saudi postings that require an existing work right.
atlas-qa.0056: EY’s Doha Assurance graduate programme read is for Qatari nationals with excellent written and spoken Arabic and English; we could not open any posting that is open to foreign graduates.
atlas-qa.0057: QatarEnergy’s graduate programme is for recent Qatari graduates, who may be posted to any QatarEnergy location; companies tied to QatarEnergy and petroleum operations are exempt from Law 12’s Qatarisation duties.
atlas-qa.0058: QIA’s one-year Journey graduate programme requires a Qatari national or the child of a Qatari mother; its international hiring is for highly experienced specialists.
atlas-qa.0059: Law 12 of 2024 makes private employers give priority to Qataris and children of Qatari women and hire expatriates only if no suitable Qatari is available; priority-group job seekers register with the Ministry of Labour.
atlas-qa.0060: Qataris are targeted at 20% of the private and semi-private workforce by 2030 under the national development strategy, after Law 12 of 2024 came into force in April 2025; IT roles for foreigners are mostly experienced hires.
atlas-qa.0061: University fairs cluster in January and February and in September and October; the pages read show no single national season and no programme with published opening months.
atlas-qa.0062: No posting or programme page read asks for a master’s degree; the national programmes read ask for being a recent graduate and, for EY, fluent Arabic and English. This is our reading.
atlas-qa.0063: Qatar Living describes a chain for every degree: the home-country higher-education authority, the home foreign ministry, the Qatari embassy, then Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs with the bonafide letter, transcript and degree. The library notes Qatar is not in the Hague Apostille Convention, and engineers and architects must also register with the Ministry of Municipality.
atlas-qa.0064: Access to fairs follows the university you attend (Education City’s is for Qatar Foundation students and alumni only; the Ouqoul graduate side is for alumni of linked Qatari universities); we found no ranking of schools by employers. This is our reading.
atlas-qa.0065: We found no apprenticeship or dual-study route into graduate jobs; the library finds no stand-alone internship visa, and Sahem part-time jobs are for current students. This is our reading.
atlas-qa.0066: State-linked bodies run the headline graduate programmes (QatarEnergy, QIA) but they are for Qataris; we found no figure for the public sector’s share of graduate hires, so for a foreign graduate the weight is our reading.
atlas-qa.0067: Residence is tied to an employer-sponsored work visa and the Ministry of Labour approves each quota; Law 12 lets employers hire expatriates only when no suitable Qatari is available, and the Ouqoul platform targets expatriate graduate roles outside the nationalisation scheme. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-qa.0068: Qatar Living’s CV guide (August 2026) says a professional headshot is commonly expected in Qatar and the Gulf, especially in the private sector and client-facing roles, though some employers treat it as optional and a few prefer none.
atlas-qa.0069: The same guide says a first-job CV should be one tight page; it also asks for nationality, date of birth and often marital status on the CV.
atlas-qa.0070: None of the programme and posting pages read mention a cover letter; EY’s nationals programme runs on an application, online assessments and a recorded video. This is our reading.
atlas-qa.0071: Qatar Living lists references as an optional last section of the CV that is commonly included; none of the programme pages read asks for them with the application.
atlas-qa.0072: A foreign degree goes through the attestation chain ending at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Qatar, and the library’s visa guide requires legalised degrees and certificates because Qatar is outside the Apostille Convention.
atlas-qa.0073: We found no page saying Qatari employers ask for a salary expectation with the first application; the contract is registered on the Ministry of Labour portal, and the legal minimum is QAR 1,000 basic plus QAR 500 housing and QAR 300 food. This is our reading for the application stage.
atlas-qa.0074: The state does the checking for a foreign hire: degrees are attested at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the library’s guide has a medical commission screening and a fingerprint record at the Ministry of Interior before the residence ID is printed.
atlas-qa.0075: Aetna’s guide calls regional recruitment informal and built on connections, with introductions valued; recruiters and agencies handle applications from abroad.
atlas-qa.0076: Applications and first interviews can be made from abroad by phone or video, and the library says the electronic work-entry visa is issued before travel; the medical test, fingerprints and ID card follow in Doha, and work cannot start on a tourist or waiver status.
atlas-qa.0077: English is the usual language of the international firms and free-zone companies, and standard contracts are registered in Arabic and English; Qatar Living says Arabic matters more for government, semi-government and some customer-facing roles. This is our reading for English at work; no source measured it.
atlas-qa.0078: EY’s Doha graduate programme for nationals runs five steps: apply, online assessments, a prerecorded video interview answering behavioural questions, a recruitment day or interview if shortlisted, then an offer. QatarEnergy says its graduate assessment may take up to 90 days.
atlas-qa.0079: From abroad, Aetna says you may have a phone or video interview with a recruiter in Qatar, and some processes include a trip to Qatar to meet key contacts over several days; Ramadan and summer slow things down. We did not establish interview dress norms or assessment-centre practice for foreign graduates.
atlas-qa.0080: Probation may last up to six months, and only once with the same employer; an employer ending it for unfitness must give at least one month’s notice. Standard contracts are registered in Arabic and English on the Ministry of Labour portal.
atlas-qa.0081: Commoner Law’s guide gives notice of one month up to two years of service and two months beyond (its own citations show a five-year threshold, so check the statute), and an end-of-service gratuity of at least three weeks of basic pay per year after one full year.
atlas-qa.0082: The legal minimum is QAR 1,000 basic plus QAR 500 for housing and QAR 300 for food, and the employer pays the work visa, medical and ID fees. We did not establish whether graduates negotiate, how long employers give to decide, or entry pay.
atlas-qa.0083: Law 12 of 2024, in force from April 2025, makes private employers give priority to Qataris and children of Qatari women; expatriates may be hired only if no suitable Qatari is available. Employers must notify the Ministry of Labour of vacancies, report new employee data every six months and train Qataris; penalties run from warnings to suspended immigration transactions and fines of up to one million riyals.
atlas-qa.0084: Companies tied to QatarEnergy and petroleum operations are exempt, and the Ministry may set a Qatari percentage for each sector once the Cabinet approves its plan. Foreign nationals were 83% of the private workforce in 2023, against a national target of 20% Qatari participation by 2030.
atlas-qa.0085: The library records that Decree-Laws 18 and 19 of 2020 removed the no-objection certificate for changing employer and Law 13 of 2018 the exit permit for most private-sector workers; the employer must still obtain the Ministry of Labour quota and the work visa. Ask early who sponsors, which entity employs you and whether the post sits inside the nationalisation scheme. This is our reading for the last point.
atlas-qa.0086: Public and platforms: the Ministry of Labour’s Ouqoul platform for private employers recruiting expatriate graduates of Qatari universities, and Jusour’s Tawzeef (an AI-assisted platform linking job seekers with employers and recruitment agencies) and Sahem (part-time student jobs and the graduate visa extension).
atlas-qa.0087: Employer pages: QatarEnergy’s careers portal (careerportal.qatarenergy.qa, graduates for Qataris), and EY Qatar’s graduate postings for nationals; we could not open the Qatar Airways, QNB or other Big Four pages.
atlas-qa.0088: University services and fairs: Qatar University’s Career Development Center (counselling, employer relations, a student-employment programme and the annual fair), the Doha Institute’s January fair, the Education City Job Fair for Qatar Foundation students and alumni, and Lusail University’s October fair. Qatar Living’s career-fairs guide lists the year’s events.
atlas-qa.0089: Applying to the national programmes (QatarEnergy graduates, QIA Journey, EY for nationals) as a foreign graduate: they require Qatari nationality or a Qatari mother.
atlas-qa.0090: Starting work, a trial day or an internship on a tourist or visa-waiver status: the library cites Law 21 of 2015, with fines up to QAR 50,000, up to three years in prison and expulsion.
atlas-qa.0091: Leaving the country after entering on the work visa but before the residence ID is printed: the library says the entry visa lapses and the process restarts.
atlas-qa.0092: Leaving the degree unattested: every degree goes through the home-country chain and the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Qatar is outside the Apostille Convention, so start the chain before the offer.
